title: Construct String with Minimum Cost
statement: Begin with an empty string `s`. In one move you choose any index `i` of `words` (indices may be chosen again and again), glue `words[i]` onto the end of `s`, and pay `costs[i]`; the arrays `words` and `costs` have equal length. Return the lowest total payment of a sequence of moves that leaves `s` exactly equal to `target`, or `-1` if no sequence of moves produces `target`.
constraints: The lengths of all words add up to at most 5 * 10^4
target and every words[i] contain only lowercase English letters
signature: int minimumCost(String target, String[] words, int[] costs)
notes:
## Intuition

Let `dp[i]` be the cheapest cost of building the first `i` letters of `target`. The last word glued on ends exactly at `i`, so `dp[i]` is the minimum of `dp[i - length] + cost` over the words that match just before `i`. Testing every word at every position (the brute force) is O(n · L) for total word length L, too slow here. An Aho–Corasick automaton (a trie of the words plus, per node, a link to its longest proper suffix in the trie) lists exactly the words ending at each position in one left-to-right pass.

## Approach

1. Insert each word into the trie `children`; `cheapest` keeps the lowest cost of a word ending at a node and `depth` its length.
2. Visit nodes breadth-first. For a `child` reached by `letter`, follow `fail` links from `fail[parent]` until a node has a `letter` edge; where it leads (or the root) is `fail[child]`. `wordLink[child]` is the nearest node on that suffix chain that ends a word.
3. Scan `target`, moving `state` the same way: fall back along `fail` until `letter` can be taken, then take it.
4. From `state` (or `wordLink[state]` if `state` ends no word), walk the word links. Each `match` is a word ending at `i`: relax `dp[i]` with `dp[i - depth[match]] + cheapest[match]`.
5. Return `dp[target.length]`, or -1 if it is still `Infinity`.

## Example 1, step by step

`target = "abcdef"`, words "abdef" (100), "abc" (1), "d" (1), "def" (10), "ef" (5). Reading "a" and "b" reaches nodes that end no word, so `dp[1]` and `dp[2]` stay `Infinity`. "c" reaches the word "abc": `dp[3] = dp[0] + 1 = 1`. "abcd" is not in the trie, so `state` falls back to the root and takes its "d" edge, a word: `dp[4] = 1 + 1 = 2`. "e" leads to "de", which ends no word. "f" leads to the word "def": `dp[6] = dp[3] + 10 = 11`; its word link "ef" gives `dp[6] = min(11, dp[4] + 5) = 7`, the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(L + n·√L): the trie and its links take O(L) amortised steps; the words ending at one position have distinct lengths, and only about √(2L) ≈ 316 distinct lengths fit in L letters.
- Space: O(L + n) for the trie, the links and `dp`.

## Pitfalls

- Several words can end at one position; stopping at the longest misses cheaper short ones, so walk the whole word-link chain.
- A plain trie walk from every start is O(n²) on a target of all `a`s with one very long word of `a`s.
- Unreachable prefixes stay `Infinity`; return -1 when `dp[target.length]` is one of them.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `children`, `cheapest`, `depth` | trie edges, cheapest word ending at a node, node's string length |
| `w`, `node`, `letter` | index of the word being inserted, its current node and letter |
| `fail` | node of the longest proper suffix that is in the trie |
| `wordLink` | nearest node on the suffix chain that ends a word (0 if none) |
| `queue`, `head`, `parent`, `child`, `link` | breadth-first construction of the links |
| `dp`, `i` | `dp[i]`: cheapest cost to build the first `i` letters of `target` |
| `state` | node of the longest suffix of the scanned text that is in the trie |
| `match` | a node whose word ends at position `i` |

narration.2: children[node] maps a letter to the next trie node; node 0 is the root, the empty string.
narration.3: cheapest[node] will hold the lowest cost of a word that ends at that node.
narration.4: depth[node] is the length of the string the node spells.
narration.5: Insert every word into the trie.
narration.8: No edge for this letter yet: create a node one letter deeper.
narration.14: Step down to the node for this letter.
narration.16: The word ends here; if it appears twice, keep the lower cost.
narration.20: Go breadth-first from the root's children, so shorter strings get their links first.
narration.23: Give each child of this node its links.
narration.25: Fall back along suffix links until some node can be extended by the same letter.
narration.28: That extension is the longest proper suffix of the child's string that is in the trie, or the root.
narration.29: The nearest word on that suffix chain: fail[child] itself if it ends a word, otherwise its own word link.
narration.33: dp[i] will be the cheapest cost to build the first i letters of target.
narration.36: Read target one letter at a time.
narration.38: If the current trie string cannot be extended by this letter, fall back to shorter suffixes.
narration.41: Take the letter; if even the root has no such edge, stay at the root.
narration.42: The first word ending here: the state itself if it is a word, otherwise its word link.
narration.43: Visit every word that ends at position i, longest first.
narration.44: Glue that word on last: build the first i - length letters, then pay its cost.
narration.45: Move on to the next shorter word ending here.
narration.48: A target that cannot be built stays at Infinity, which the problem reports as -1.
